case_name: K.N. Mehra v. State of Rajasthan

pages.text:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
K.N. Mehra ... Appellant
versus
State of Rajasthan ... Respondent
Coram: B. Jagannadhadas, B.P. Sinha, P. Govinda Menon, JJ.
Judgment Dated: 11 February 1957

JAGANNADHADAS, J.:
1. The appellant, an Indian Air Force cadet undergoing training at Jodhpur, flew an aircraft without authority and flew across the border to Pakistan. He was convicted of theft under Section 379 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. Decision on Dishonest Intent: Theft does not require permanent deprivation of property. Even a temporary taking of property dishonestly, causing wrongful gain to oneself or wrongful loss to the lawful owner (Indian Air Force), satisfies Section 378 IPC. Taking off and flying the aircraft without consent was an unlawful moving with dishonest intent. Conviction under Section 379 affirmed.
